questions.prompt: What does an MCP server fundamentally give a coding agent?
choices: A list of named functions with JSON schemas that the agent may call, plus the results, over a simple RPC protocol
questions.explanation: The Model Context Protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0 with a small vocabulary: initialize, tools/list, tools/call (and resources, prompts). Everything the agent can do to your systems is the union of the tools servers expose.

questions.prompt: Why must a stdio MCP server write nothing but protocol messages to stdout?
choices: The client parses every stdout line as JSON-RPC; a stray print breaks the session, so logs go to stderr
questions.explanation: stdio transport is newline-delimited JSON on stdout. Debug output on stdout corrupts the stream; stderr is free for logs.

questions.prompt: An agent asks for `list_pods` in namespace `prod`, which is not on the allow-list. What should the server return?
choices: Run it anyway; the agent knows best
A tools/call result with isError: true explaining the refusal, so the model can choose an allowed namespace
A JSON-RPC error that closes the connection
questions.explanation: Tool-level problems (bad arguments, policy refusals, kubectl failures) are results with isError so the model can recover; JSON-RPC errors are for protocol problems like an unknown method or tool.

questions.prompt: Why does the server build the kubectl argv itself from typed arguments instead of accepting a `command` string?
choices: Because a free-form command lets the model (or a prompt injection in a log line it read) run anything; building argv from a schema makes the read-only guarantee structural
questions.explanation: Agents read untrusted text (logs, events, tickets). If any of it can steer a shell string, the tool is a remote shell. Typed arguments plus a verb allow-list and forbidden flags keep the surface read-only no matter what the model is told.

questions.prompt: You add a `rollout_restart` write tool. Where should the human approval live?
choices: In the server, which prompts on its own stdin
In the client (Claude Code, Cursor, your CI gate), which can show the user the exact call and get a yes before tools/call is sent; the server still logs and can require a confirm argument
questions.explanation: The server's stdin is the protocol stream, so it cannot talk to the human. Clients own approval UX; servers own policy (allow-lists, audit logs, idempotent operations) and should assume the client might be misconfigured.

questions.prompt: The output of list_events for a busy cluster is 400 KB. What is the right behaviour?
choices: Truncate at a limit with a hint to narrow the query (namespace, warnings_only, tail_lines); context windows and token cost are part of the tool's contract
questions.explanation: Every byte a tool returns is read by the model. Bounded output with a clear hint keeps the agent useful and cheap, and nudges it toward the narrower calls a human SRE would make.
